To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed an end to end technique to segment multiple retinal pathologic lesions simultaneously using fully convolutional neural networks and the proposed algorithm has been shown to outperform existing techniques in terms of accuracy.
we have developed a novel fully convolutional deep neural network architecture for simultaneous segmentation of exudates, microaneurysms, and cotton wool spot.
we have proposed an end to end technique which is capable of segmenting three types of retinal pathologys simultaneously and the proposed technique has achieved state of the arth accuracies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient and effective algorithm for simultaneous segmentation of retinal exudates, retinal hemorrhages, and retinal cotton wool spots.
the development of an automated system that can simultaneously extract multiple retinal pathologic lesions.
the development of automated retinal pathology segmentation framework which can be used in the diagnosis and treatment of various systemic, cardiovascular and ophthalmic disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our proposed algorithm has the potential to be used as a stand-alone diagnostic system for the detection of various retinal pathologies and may aid in the early detection of systemic diseases such as hypertension, diabetes and cardiovascular diseases.
the proposed technique is able to segment all three retinal pathologies simultaneously with state of the art accuracy.

the proposed algorithm is capable of simultaneously extracting multiple retinal pathologic features from retinal fundus image and may aid in the diagnosis of various systemic, cardiovascular and ophthalmic pathologies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed technique has been able to segment multiple retinal pathologic structures with high accuracy and can be further extended for segmentation of other retinal pathologies as well.
the proposed technique is a step forward in the direction of automated retinal pathologic extraction for various systemic, cardiac, and ocular diseases.
the proposed technique may be useful for simultaneous detection of multiple retinal abnormalities and hence may aid in the development of a robust automated diagnostic system.

the proposed algorithm can be used as an efficient tool for simultaneous segmentation of retinal exudates, cotton wool spots, and hemorrhages.

the developed approach may aid the clinicians to perform simultaneous segmentation of multiple pathologies which may further help in early diagnosis and prognosis of systemic and cardiovascular diseases.
the proposed algorithm may aid in simultaneous detection and quantification of multiple retinal pathology in a fully automated fashion.
